Our goal is to generate a natural language summary which articulates S_e, the set of selected opinions. To achieve this, we need a natural language generation (NLG) model which takes a set of opinion phrases as input and produces a fluent, review-like summary as output.

We conducted user study via crowdsourcing using the FigureEight platform. To ensure the quality of annotators, we used a dedicated expert-worker pool provided by FigureEight.

Annotators were asked to judge summaries based on informativeness, coherence, non-redundancy (best-worst), content support level (full/partial/none), and aspect coverage (exclusive/partial/none).

We asked the annotators to select the best and worst summaries w.r.t. the following criteria: • Informativeness: How much useful information about the business does the summary provide? • Coherence: How coherent and easy to read is the summary? • Non-redanduncy: Is the summary successful at avoiding redundant and repeated opinions?
